summary: Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. Educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, he was founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987) and Centenary Professor at Calcutta (1971).
Nirupam Chakma specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where he was supervised by Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Nitin Kumar Jain is an Indologist who earned his PhD from Central Sanskrit University. In 2019, he held a post there as an Assistant Professor.
Nivitigala Sumitta Thero works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of the West (2014–2023) and became Founder and CEO of Dhamma USA in 2022.
Noa Gal is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her DPhil from the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied at Wolfson College, Oxford, earning a D.Phil. under Richard Gombrich, and also studied under Shlomo Biderman. She was a lecturer and research fellow at Stanford (attested 2005).
Noah Avigan is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He has been a graduate student and held a post in Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (B.A., M.A., Litt.D. 1993). He taught at the University of Tokyo (Professor Emeritus 1981–1994) and Taisho University (~1994–2008).

Noboru Miyata (1936–2000) was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, he served as Professor of Folklore at Tsukuba (~1976–1999) and taught at Kanagawa University (~1999–2000).
Noboru Ueda works in Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, Hajime Sakurabe, and others, he served as a professor at Otani University (~1988–2014) and president of its junior college.

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and under Yutaka Ochihara, later holding posts at the University of Toronto (attested 1969), Kyoto University (attested 1979), and Taisho University (attested 2026).

Nobuhiro Ota (b. 1969) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. Since 2002, he has taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, becoming a professor in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied as a research student at Taisho University and held a post as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi (b. 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his studies at Rissho University in 1959 and later served as an assistant professor there (attested 1972).

Tensho Miyazaki (b. 1978) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo and held posts at Toyo University (~2011–2014) and the University of Tokyo (attested 2015).

Nobumi Iyanaga (b. 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and later held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient's Tokyo Centre (2008–2014).
Nobuo Otsuka (b. 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and served there as a researcher (attested 1995).

Nobuyoshi Yamabe (b. 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Osaka, Otani, and Yale (PhD under Stanley Weinstein), later holding professorships at Tokyo University of Agriculture (2003) and Waseda University (appointed 2015).

Nobuyuki Kaji (b. 1936) is a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University and earned a Litt.D. from Tohoku University. He was a professor at Osaka University (1984–1998) and later held posts at Doshisha and Ritsumeikan universities.
